item.title: Muroji: The Mountain Temple of Women — Guide
item.description: Muroji, hidden in the wooded mountains of eastern Nara near Uda, is one of the prefecture’s most atmospheric temples, an ancient Shingon complex set beside a mountain stream and climbing the forested slope on moss-covered stone stairways. It became known as the ‘Women’s Koya’ (Nyonin Koya) because, unlike the great monastery of Mount Koya, it welcomed women pilgrims. Its jewel is a small, exquisitely proportioned five-story pagoda, among the oldest and smallest in Japan, and the temple is celebrated for its natural setting — a blaze of rhododendrons in spring, fresh green in summer and brilliant maple colour in autumn.

item.title: Nara Hidden Gems: Asuka, Muro-ji, Tanzan Shrine & Ancient Sites Beyond the Park
item.description: The Nara that most visitors see — the deer, Todai-ji, Kasuga Taisha — represents perhaps 10% of the prefecture’s heritage. Spread across the Yamato Plain and into the surrounding mountains is a landscape of extraordinary archaeological and cultural density: Japan’s first capitals, the oldest Buddhist temples, burial mounds that predate written Japanese history, mountain shrines of mythological antiquity, and a merchant town so intact it makes Kyoto’s Gion feel modern. These are the sites that reward the traveller willing to go one train stop further.
